Instead of this, let's add a "data stride" parameter to `raytracing_pipeline_get_shader_group_handles` function, so it increments the data pointer using that value instead of the shader group stride from the raytracing capability struct. 

The reason the function accepts a hit index array is to avoid calling the virtual function in a loop in the first place.
Same as above, shouldn't be necessary.

I am not sure about that. If we do not zero-fill this data, there would be uninitialized bytes between _handle size_ and _stride_, and uploading garbage data to GPU buffers does not feel right. I could actually get rid of the `memset` and use `resize_initialized`.
These bytes would be unused, though. GPUs are not supposed to access bytes beyond the shader group handle size when looking up which one to execute.
